turns.content:
We are preparing Northstar Home's four-week holiday overflow-fulfillment plan. Read `demand_forecast.csv`, `capacity_note.md`, and `partner_sheet.md`, and use only those workspace files for factual claims; do not browse or add outside facts. This is the initial review turn, so do not create the final plan yet. In at most five bullets, calculate the weekly overflow under both the base and stress forecasts, identify the external partner the packet most strongly supports, and flag at least two material uncertainties.

Retain these instructions for the eventual plan: cover all four forecast weeks; keep sourced facts separate from recommendations; label observed results, forecasts, and supplier projections accurately; cite factual claims with `[Demand Forecast]`, `[Capacity Note]`, or `[Partner Sheet]`; and state uncertainty without presenting assumptions as facts. Stop after the bullets and wait for my clarification.

Clarification for the final plan: use the base forecast, select Meridian Fulfillment as the external partner, and allocate each week's overflow 65% to Meridian and 35% to internal overtime. Apply Meridian's setup fee once, include all incremental handling costs, and exclude returns, rework, and downstream freight as the packet directs. Keep the four listed weeks and the 12,000-unit baseline capacity.

The eventual file must be 550–750 words and use exactly these headings in order: `# Q4 Overflow Fulfillment Plan`, `## Decision summary`, `## Sourced facts`, `## Recommendation`, `## Weekly allocation`, `## Cost estimate`, `## Uncertainty`, and `## Actions`. Under Sourced facts, use a table to distinguish observed evidence, forecasts, and supplier projections from one another. Do not create `operations_plan.md` yet; briefly confirm whether this allocation fits the stated Meridian and overtime limits, then wait.

Correction: allocate each week's overflow 75% to Meridian Fulfillment and 25% to internal overtime, not 65% and 35%. This replaces only the allocation split from my clarification. Preserve the base forecast, Meridian selection, four weeks, baseline capacity, one-time setup-fee treatment, cost inclusions and exclusions, source-only rule, citations, fact/recommendation separation, uncertainty treatment, word range, headings, and every other non-conflicting instruction.

Continue to hold off on creating `operations_plan.md`; confirm the corrected split and whether it fits both capacity limits, then wait for the final request.

Now create the substantive final result in `operations_plan.md` using the complete accumulated instructions and the corrected 75%/25% split. Do not mention the superseded split.

Under Decision summary, give exactly three bullets covering the planning basis, chosen partner, and corrected allocation. Under Sourced facts, provide a Markdown table with columns `Fact`, `Evidence type`, and `Source`; include the capacity baseline, all four base forecasts, the overtime limit and prior pilot result, Meridian's capacity and fees, and its on-time projection. Make the evidence-type cells explicitly distinguish `Observed`, `Forecast`, `Operating limit`, `Proposal term`, and `Supplier projection`. Keep recommendations out of that section.

Under Recommendation, give the rationale for the plan and explain the capacity headroom. Under Weekly allocation, use one Markdown table with columns `Week of`, `Forecast units`, `Baseline capacity`, `Overflow`, `Meridian (75%)`, and `Overtime (25%)`, with one row per week in date order and a total row. Under Cost estimate, use a two-column `Item` and `Amount` table with exactly these rows in order: `Meridian handling`, `Meridian setup`, `Overtime handling`, and `Total incremental cost`; show dollars with commas and two decimal places, and state immediately below the table which costs are excluded.

Under Uncertainty, include exactly three bullets. Each must identify an uncertainty, explain its operational impact, and give a response framed as a recommendation rather than a sourced fact. Under Actions, include exactly four numbered actions, each with an owner and a due date; these actions are recommendations. Do not add any other headings or create any other file. Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`; if it passes, respond with the complete contents of `operations_plan.md`, not a description of what you did.
